start.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
start.text: Welcome to the table. Cards are honest. Players are usually more complicated. What can I do for you?

choices.text: Teach me how this table works.
How long have you worked here?

learn-table.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
learn-table.text: Simple goal: get closer to twenty-one than the house without going over. The interesting part is deciding when to stop.

choices.text: What is the safest way to play?
What should I watch for at the table?

learn-table-end-1.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
learn-table-end-1.text: Safe is relative, but patience beats panic. Learn the basic decisions before you start chasing luck.

learn-table-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
learn-table-end-2.text: Watch the dealer's up-card, your own total, and the mood of the table. People reveal plenty when money starts moving.

learn-table-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
learn-table-end-3.text: Take a seat when you're ready. Once the cards are out, hesitation gets expensive.

ask-rumors.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-rumors.text: Rumors? In a casino? Never. But the VIP room has been busier than usual, and not everyone going in looks like a high roller.

choices.text: Who has been going into VIP?

ask-rumors-end-1.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-rumors-end-1.text: A few regulars, one nervous staffer, and someone security pretended not to notice.

ask-rumors-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-rumors-end-2.text: That is exactly the sort of question that makes dealers suddenly remember they have cards to shuffle.

ask-rumors-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-rumors-end-3.text: Probably wise. Curiosity is cheap until someone notices it.

ask-dealer.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-dealer.text: Long enough to know every table has two games: the one printed on the felt and the one happening between the people.

ask-dealer-end-1.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-dealer-end-1.text: The second one. Cards decide a hand. People decide what happens after.

ask-dealer-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-dealer-end-2.text: Most nights. The casino is predictable right up until it isn't.

ask-dealer-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-dealer-end-3.text: Know where the exits are, tip the bartender, and never assume a smiling bear is relaxed.

start.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
start.text: Good evening. Keep your hands where the cameras can see them and we will get along beautifully.

choices.text: You pay a lot of attention to the cameras.
How do you spot a cheater?
Anything unusual happen on your shift?

ask-cameras.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-cameras.text: Occupational habit. Security watches the cards, the chips, the doors, and especially anyone who thinks they are not being watched.

ask-cameras-end-1.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-cameras-end-1.text: If I knew one, I would not announce it across a blackjack table.

ask-cameras-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-cameras-end-2.text: They miss things. Everyone does. The trick is knowing whether it was a mistake or permission.

ask-cameras-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-cameras-end-3.text: Of course not. Nobody ever is.

ask-cheating.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-cheating.text: Patterns. Strange bets. Partners who never look at each other. People who become very calm at exactly the wrong moment.

choices.text: What happens when you catch one?

ask-cheating-end-1.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-cheating-end-1.text: I stop the game. Security decides whether the conversation continues somewhere quieter.

ask-cheating-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-cheating-end-2.text: Important people are rarely caught. They are usually escorted.

ask-cheating-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-cheating-end-3.text: For a hand? Certainly. For long? That is a much harder profession.

ask-shift.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-shift.text: A chip tray came up short, then balanced itself ten minutes later. Money does not usually apologize and return on its own.

choices.text: Who had access to the tray?

ask-shift-end-1.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-shift-end-1.text: Dealer, pit staff, cashier, and anyone clever enough to make that list incomplete.

ask-shift-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-shift-end-2.text: Naturally. The report disappeared faster than the chips did.

ask-shift-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-shift-end-3.text: Maybe. Or maybe the casino has learned to steal from itself.

start.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
start.text: You look like someone deciding whether to gamble or ask questions. Questions are cheaper, for now.

choices.text: What do you know about the VIP room?
Who should I talk to around here?

ask-vip.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-vip.text: Enough to stay out of it. High rollers go in through the front. Problems seem to leave through the staff side.

ask-vip-end-1.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-vip-end-1.text: Debts, arguments, people who suddenly decide they have somewhere else to be.

ask-vip-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-vip-end-2.text: Officially, management. Unofficially, whoever security was told not to bother.

ask-vip-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-vip-end-3.text: Not directly. But people with the right story sometimes find doors opening for them.

ask-regulars.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-regulars.text: The bartender hears everything, the cashier remembers amounts, and roulette remembers faces. Pick the kind of truth you need.

ask-regulars-end-1.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-regulars-end-1.text: People talk when they drink, and bartenders learn to listen without looking curious.

ask-regulars-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-regulars-end-2.text: Chips become money there. Money leaves a trail, even when people try not to.

ask-regulars-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-regulars-end-3.text: Same crowd every night. A dealer notices when a familiar face stops showing up.

ask-warning.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-warning.text: Do not follow staff through locked doors unless you know why you are doing it. And do not owe favors to security.

choices.text: What is behind the staff doors?

ask-warning-end-2.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-warning-end-2.text: Mostly boring things. The dangerous part is the one boring thing someone does not want you to see.

ask-warning-end-3.speaker: Blackjack Dealer
ask-warning-end-3.text: Everybody says that before the casino tests the claim.

start.speaker: Roulette Dealer
start.text: Red, black, odd, even. Everyone wants the wheel to tell them something about the future. What are you hoping to hear?

choices.text: Is there any way to read the wheel?
You recognize most of the regulars?

ask-wheel.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-wheel.text: You can read people. The wheel is less cooperative. Anyone promising certainty is selling something.

ask-wheel-end-1.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-wheel-end-1.text: There are ways to manage risk. There is no conversation that makes probability sentimental.

ask-wheel-end-2.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-wheel-end-2.text: Always. Birthdays, anniversaries, room numbers, old mistakes.

ask-wheel-end-3.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-wheel-end-3.text: Whichever one keeps you entertained without making you desperate.

ask-regular.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-regular.text: The serious ones. A guest used to bet the same corner every night, then vanished three nights ago.

choices.text: Where did they usually go afterward?

ask-regular-end-1.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-regular-end-1.text: A quiet bear in a charcoal suit. Never drank. Always cashed out exactly one stack at a time.

ask-regular-end-2.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-regular-end-2.text: Security notices everything. Whether they act is a different question.

ask-regular-end-3.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-regular-end-3.text: Toward the cashier, then the lounge. After that, I had a wheel to watch.

ask-luck.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-luck.text: I believe people call it luck when they cannot see the machinery underneath.

ask-luck-end-1.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-luck-end-1.text: It is a casino. Cynicism is just optimism with receipts.

ask-luck-end-2.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-luck-end-2.text: No. Randomness is real. So are people trying to take credit for it.

ask-luck-end-3.speaker: Roulette Dealer
ask-luck-end-3.text: Then make sure tomorrow morning still belongs to you.

start.speaker: Poker Host
start.text: Table's open. Poker is mostly a conversation where the chips do the shouting.

choices.text: What makes a good poker player?
Why is this table so quiet?

ask-poker.speaker: Poker Host
ask-poker.text: Patience, memory, and the ability to look bored while your brain is on fire.

choices.text: What should I watch in other players?
How much is bluffing really used?

ask-poker-end-1.speaker: Poker Host
ask-poker-end-1.text: Timing. Hands. Breathing. And the stories they tell with their bets.

ask-poker-end-2.speaker: Poker Host
ask-poker-end-2.text: Less than movies suggest, more than nervous players hope.

ask-poker-end-3.speaker: Poker Host
ask-poker-end-3.text: Sit a few hands, bet small, and explain every decision to yourself. That is a better teacher than bravado.

ask-tournament.speaker: Poker Host
ask-tournament.text: Small ones on ordinary nights. Private games happen too, but invitations travel quietly.

ask-tournament-end-1.speaker: Poker Host
ask-tournament-end-1.text: Play consistently, do not cause problems, and make someone think your presence is useful.

ask-tournament-end-2.speaker: Poker Host
ask-tournament-end-2.text: Officially? The casino. In practice, the guest with the deepest stack usually sets the temperature.

ask-tournament-end-3.speaker: Poker Host
ask-tournament-end-3.text: Sometimes VIP. Sometimes somewhere that does not appear on the public floor plan.

ask-table.speaker: Poker Host
ask-table.text: Because the loud players already lost. The ones still sitting have learned not to advertise.

choices.text: Anyone here I should worry about?
What do you notice about me?

ask-table-end-1.speaker: Poker Host
ask-table-end-1.text: Worry is inefficient. Pay attention instead.

ask-table-end-2.speaker: Poker Host
ask-table-end-2.text: You ask before you bet. That already makes you unusual.

ask-table-end-3.speaker: Poker Host
ask-table-end-3.text: Take a seat. Your first lesson starts when you think you have a good hand.

start.speaker: Poker Dealer
start.text: High-stakes side of the floor. If you came for easy money, the exit is still behind you.

choices.text: How high do the stakes get?
I heard about a private game.

ask-highstakes.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-highstakes.text: Higher than the signs admit. Some games are played for chips. Others are played for access, favors, and silence.

choices.text: How do I get into one?

ask-highstakes-end-1.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-highstakes-end-1.text: Introductions. Information. Doors opening after hours.

ask-highstakes-end-2.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-highstakes-end-2.text: People who do not enjoy being described by dealers.

ask-highstakes-end-3.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-highstakes-end-3.text: First become useful. Money gets attention; usefulness gets invitations.

ask-marked.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-marked.text: Once. The marks were almost perfect. The player using them was not.

ask-marked-end-1.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-marked-end-1.text: Security took them away from the table. I never saw them play here again.

ask-marked-end-2.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-marked-end-2.text: The cards were too clean in exactly the same places.

ask-marked-end-3.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-marked-end-3.text: Maybe. But cheating a casino means defeating people whose full-time job is expecting you.

ask-private.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-private.text: Then you heard the first rule: people talk. The second rule is that nobody admits the game exists.

ask-private-end-1.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-private-end-1.text: Start with the bar. Ask about the bear who orders sparkling water and never sits.

ask-private-end-2.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-private-end-2.text: Late enough that the tourists are gone, early enough that morning staff has not arrived.

ask-private-end-3.speaker: Poker Dealer
ask-private-end-3.text: Good instinct. Private games are usually expensive before the first card is dealt.

start.speaker: Casino Cashier
start.text: Chips in, money out, receipts if you want them. What are we doing today?

ask-cashing.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-cashing.text: Give me the chips, I verify the amount, and we settle the value. Large transactions get extra attention.

choices.text: Can I cash out someone else's chips?

ask-cashing-end-1.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-cashing-end-1.text: Large enough that paperwork becomes part of the experience.

ask-cashing-end-2.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-cashing-end-2.text: Chips move between people all the time. Suspicious patterns are another matter.

ask-cashing-end-3.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-cashing-end-3.text: The casino keeps more records than most guests imagine.

ask-strange.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-strange.text: One guest has been converting small stacks repeatedly instead of making one large cash-out. That is unusual behavior.

choices.text: Do you know who it is?

ask-strange-end-1.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-strange-end-1.text: Could be nerves. Could be a habit. Could be someone trying not to make one transaction look important.

ask-strange-end-2.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-strange-end-2.text: I know the face. I do not give customer details to strangers.

ask-strange-end-3.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-strange-end-3.text: Anything unusual gets noted. What happens after that is above my window.

ask-comps.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-comps.text: Play generates attention, attention generates offers. Rooms, meals, access. The casino likes loyal guests.

choices.text: Can comps get me into VIP?
Who is the best host to talk to?
Can you add comps to my account?

ask-comps-end-1.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-comps-end-1.text: Enough play can open some doors. Other doors require a host.

ask-comps-end-2.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-comps-end-2.text: Ask at the bar during the quieter hours. Hosts tend to circulate where guests linger.

ask-comps-end-3.speaker: Casino Cashier
ask-comps-end-3.text: Not from this window. I handle value, not affection.

start.speaker: Bartender
start.text: Welcome to the lounge. I pour drinks, hear stories, and forget names on request. What will it be?

choices.text: I'm looking for information, not a drink.
You seem to know everything that happens here.

ask-rumor.speaker: Bartender
ask-rumor.text: Information costs more, mostly because people regret giving it away. What are you looking for?

ask-rumor-end-1.speaker: Bartender
ask-rumor-end-1.text: VIP has had a late-night crowd lately. Same faces, same corner, lots of conversations that stop when staff walks by.

ask-rumor-end-2.speaker: Bartender
ask-rumor-end-2.text: Security has been rotating patrols more often. Either management is nervous or somebody wants the floor to feel nervous.

ask-rumor-end-3.speaker: Bartender
ask-rumor-end-3.text: A service door near the staff area has been opening after closing time. I know because the same three guests arrive here right afterward.

ask-regulars.speaker: Bartender
ask-regulars.text: Depends what you mean by interesting. Rich, dangerous, lonely, or useful?

ask-regulars-end-1.speaker: Bartender
ask-regulars-end-1.text: Talk to the cashier if you need numbers. Roulette if you need faces. Me if you need connections.

ask-regulars-end-2.speaker: Bartender
ask-regulars-end-2.text: The dangerous ones rarely look dangerous. Watch who other people make room for.

ask-regulars-end-3.speaker: Bartender
ask-regulars-end-3.text: Half the casino. Loneliness keeps bar stools warm and slot machines busy.

ask-bartender.speaker: Bartender
ask-bartender.text: Not everything. Just what people say when they believe the person holding the glass is furniture.

ask-bartender-end-1.speaker: Bartender
ask-bartender-end-1.text: Only to keep trouble from spilling across my bar.

ask-bartender-end-2.speaker: Bartender
ask-bartender-end-2.text: Best seat in the building. Everybody eventually comes through the lounge.

ask-bartender-end-3.speaker: Bartender
ask-bartender-end-3.text: Trust is a large order. Start with a small question.
